index.meta.title: Sprocket Player — Your media, your way. On Apple TV and iPad.
index.meta.description: Sprocket Player is a media browser and player for Apple TV and iPad. Plays the movies, shows, photos and documents you already own from your Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server or straight from your NAS. Direct play first, HDR on Apple TV, no subscription, no cloud library.
hero.lede: Sprocket Player plays the movies, shows, photos and documents you already own, from your Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server or straight from the shares on your home network. No subscription. No cloud library. Your media stays yours.
hero.requirements: Requires tvOS 18.6 or iPadOS 17.6 or later.
formats.lede: Two video engines, VLC and MPV, give you the final say over picture quality, from HDR output on Apple TV to fine-grained picture tuning, and between them they play the MKVs, remuxes and odd containers that trip up other players. One app, all your media.
formats.video.title: Video
formats.video.body: Full-bitrate playback with multiple audio tracks, chapters, and embedded and external subtitle support.
formats.photos.title: Photos
formats.photos.body: Browse your photos from a network folder or your iCloud Photos library, or sit back and enjoy them as a slideshow. Any photo can become your wallpaper.
formats.docs.title: Documents & comics
formats.docs.body: Read PDFs, comic archives and text files from the couch, with page-by-page navigation on the Siri Remote or touch.
formats.sources: Sources: Plex, Jellyfin and Emby servers, SMB and NFS network shares, plus the on-device Photos library. Shares and servers on your network are discovered automatically.
companion.title_b: Plex, Jellyfin, Emby and Kodi libraries.
companion.lede: Your library, anywhere you want it to be. Whether you run a popular media server or prefer a network file share, Sprocket lets you enjoy your library with no compromises.
companion.point1: Sign in to Plex, Jellyfin or Emby and your movies and shows are there, with the posters, descriptions and episode details you already know.
companion.point2: No media server? Point Sprocket at a shared folder on your NAS or computer. Posters and descriptions saved alongside your files by Kodi and similar library tools show up automatically.
companion.point3: Videos play in their original quality. If you use a media server, it can step in and convert a file that otherwise wouldn't play, and Sprocket tells you when that happens.
companion.point4: Pick up where you left off. Sprocket remembers what you've watched and can hide it with one toggle.
companion.point5: Keep a film series together. On a shared folder, Collections gather every movie in a franchise into one place.
companion.plex: Sign in with a short code.
companion.caption: Your library, on the big screen.
intro.lede: Turn on Intro Detection and Sprocket finds the opening titles in your shows for you. When they start, a Skip Intro button appears. One press and you're into the episode.
intro.point1: Works with the shows you already have. Nothing to download, and nothing to install on your server.
intro.point2: Private by design. It all happens on your Apple TV or iPad.
intro.point3: New episodes are covered automatically as you add them.
intro.point4: Off until you want it. Switch it on in Options.
intro.caption: Straight to the story.
direct.lede: Sprocket plays your videos in their original quality, from wherever they live. Use what you already have and it just works. And when a video needs a hand, a media server can convert it for you.
direct.point1: Simplest: use what you have. A media server or a shared folder, Sprocket is at home with either.
direct.point2: Fastest: a shared folder with your library already organised. Nothing sits between Sprocket and your files, so browsing and playback are at their quickest.
direct.point3: Older Apple TV, or watching away from home? A media server can convert video to suit the device and the connection.
direct.point4: Two video engines, VLC and MPV. Choose the one that looks best on your setup, with HDR on Apple TV 4K.
direct.caption: Multiple audio tracks and subtitles, a swipe away.
privacy.lede: No account to create. No tracking. Nobody looking over your shoulder. Sprocket connects to your media, and that is where it stops.
privacy.pin.title: Encrypted, always
privacy.pin.body: Thumbnails and details Sprocket keeps on your device are always encrypted. Add a PIN to anything you'd rather keep to yourself and it's locked tighter still.
privacy.disconnect.title: Walks away when you do
privacy.disconnect.body: Sprocket can disconnect when you leave the app or go idle, so a shared living-room TV stays a shared TV.
privacy.note: Sprocket only talks to the places you point it at. If you use Plex, that includes your Plex account, which signs you in and helps Sprocket find your server. Cast photos are the one exception: they load from the web addresses saved in your library's files. Passwords and sign-ins are kept in your device's secure Keychain. Crash reports are off unless you turn them on.
privacy.caption: Your sign-in details never leave the device.
more.lede: Small things that add up to an app you actually want to open every night.
more.devices.title: Apple TV and iPad
more.devices.body: One app, designed for the Siri Remote at ten feet and for touch on the couch. Same library either way.
more.wallpapers.title: Wallpapers
more.wallpapers.body: Bundled photo and animated backgrounds, or long-press any photo in your library and make it the wallpaper.
more.sort.title: Sort your way
more.sort.body: Name, date, size, recently viewed or random. Favourites float to the top, and each folder remembers how you sorted it.
more.collections.title: Collections
more.collections.body: Group every film in a franchise on a file share into one folder, even the later ones that stopped following the naming pattern.

gallery.tv_docs: Comics and PDFs, page by page.

support.faq.q1: Which devices does Sprocket Player run on?
support.faq.a1: Apple TV running tvOS 18.6 or later, and iPad running iPadOS 17.6 or later. It is not available for iPhone.
support.faq.q2: Does Sprocket Player need Plex, Jellyfin or Emby installed?
support.faq.a2: No. A shared folder on your NAS or computer works on its own, and Sprocket shows any posters and descriptions saved alongside your files. If you already run Plex, Jellyfin or Emby, sign in and Sprocket uses the server's library and artwork directly.
support.faq.q3: Sprocket can't connect to a share on my Windows PC. What should I check?
support.faq.a3: Sprocket Player needs SMB version 2 or later. If SMB2 has been turned off on the PC, turn it back on in Windows and try again. Also check that file sharing is enabled and that the user name and password are correct.
support.faq.a4: Entirely on the device. Sign-in details live in the system Keychain, and saved thumbnails and library details are always encrypted. See the

more.phone.title: Set up from your phone
more.phone.body: Scan the QR code on your Apple TV and fill in the address, name and PIN on your phone's keyboard. Sign in to Plex or Jellyfin with a short code, never a password on the remote.
more.picture.title: Picture controls
more.picture.body: Aspect, deinterlace, speed, brightness and colour, plus upscaling, debanding and tone mapping on the MPV engine. Adjust live while the picture plays, per file if you like.
gallery.signin: Sign in with a code. Nothing typed on the remote.
download.localised: Available in English, French, German, Italian, Spanish and Japanese.
support.faq.q5: How do I sign in to Plex or Jellyfin on Apple TV?
support.faq.a5: Choose Authenticate on the Add Source form. The TV shows a short code and a QR code. Approve the code at plex.tv/link or in any signed-in Jellyfin client, and the TV finishes on its own. If a Jellyfin administrator has switched Quick Connect off, choose Use a Password Instead. Emby uses the phone setup form.
support.faq.q6: Why did a video play as a converted stream?
support.faq.a6: On a media server, Sprocket plays the original file whenever it can. It asks the server to convert only when this device can't decode the codec, the connection is too slow for the file, or the server is outside your network. A notice says which.

privacy.account.body: There is no Sprocket account to sign up for and no Sprocket cloud. Your library goes from your home to your screen, with nobody in between.

policy.meta.title: Privacy Policy — Sprocket Player
policy.meta.description: What Sprocket Player stores, what it connects to, and what it never does. No account, no tracking, no cloud.
policy.title: Sprocket Player Privacy Policy
policy.intro: Sprocket Player is a media browser and player for Apple TV and iPad. This policy explains what the app stores, what it connects to, and what it never does.
policy.short.title: The short version
policy.short.li1: There is no Sprocket account and no Sprocket server. We do not receive your media, your library, or your viewing activity.
policy.short.li2: The app connects only to the file shares and media servers you add, and to your Plex account if you use Plex. The one exception, cast photos, is described below.
policy.short.li3: There is no advertising, no tracking and no usage analytics.
policy.short.li4: Crash reports are off by default and are sent only if you turn them on.
policy.device.title: What is stored on your device
policy.device.p1: Everything Sprocket Player remembers is kept on the device you use it on:
policy.device.li1: Passwords for your file shares and sign-in tokens for your media servers are stored in the system Keychain.
policy.device.li2_lead: Your library, as you left it.
policy.device.li2: The list of sources you added, your settings, what you have watched and where you stopped.
policy.device.li3: Thumbnails, and the titles and descriptions shown in the library, are saved so the app doesn't have to fetch them again.
policy.device.p2: Saved thumbnails and library details are always encrypted on the device, using a key that never leaves it. If you protect a source with a PIN, that PIN becomes part of the key, so those items cannot be read without it.
policy.connect.title: What the app connects to
policy.connect.p1: Sprocket Player connects to the places you tell it to. The one exception is cast photos, described below.
policy.connect.shares.title: Your local network
policy.connect.shares.body: With your permission, the app looks on your local network for file shares (SMB, NFS) and media servers (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby) so it can offer them to you, and connects to the ones you add. Your device will ask you to allow local network access the first time this is needed.
policy.connect.servers.title: Your media servers
policy.connect.servers.p1: When you add a Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server, the app signs in to it and asks it for your library, artwork and video. Along with your sign-in, the server receives the app's name and version, a device label, and a random identifier created for this installation, so that the server can list Sprocket Player among your authorised devices. That identifier is not shared with anyone else.
policy.connect.servers.p2: Your server keeps its own records of what is requested from it, under its own settings and its own privacy terms. Sprocket Player keeps its own record of what you have watched on your device and does not read or change the watched status on your server. If you connect to a server outside your home network, that connection travels over the internet to that server.
policy.connect.plex.title: Your Plex account
policy.connect.plex.p1: Plex sign-in is handled by Plex's own service at plex.tv, not by your server. If you use Plex, the app contacts plex.tv when you sign in with a code, when you choose which of your servers to add, and each time it connects to a server added that way, to look up the server's current address.
policy.connect.plex.p2_before: What Plex does with those requests is described in
policy.connect.plex.p2_after: . Jellyfin and Emby sign-in happens directly with your own server and involves no outside service. If you do not use Plex, the app never contacts plex.tv.
policy.connect.phone.title: Setting up from your phone
policy.connect.phone.body: On Apple TV you can scan a QR code to fill in a connection form on your phone. While that form is open, the Apple TV serves a single page to your local network. What you type is encrypted in your phone's browser with a key carried in the QR code, and is sent only to your Apple TV. The page stops being available as soon as the form closes. Nothing is sent outside your network.
policy.connect.cast.title: Cast photos
policy.connect.cast.body: Library files written by tools such as Kodi can include web addresses for photos of the cast. When you open the cast list for a movie or show on a file share, the app downloads those photos from the addresses in your files. The site that hosts them receives your device's internet address and the photos requested. The photos are held in memory only and are never saved to your device. If your files contain no such addresses, no request is made.
policy.connect.nothing.title: What the app does not do
policy.connect.nothing.body: Sprocket Player does not send the contents of your library to any online service to identify or look up your media. Posters and descriptions come from your own server or from files saved alongside your media. Features such as intro detection and thumbnail generation run entirely on your device.
policy.photos.title: Your photo library
policy.photos.body: If you allow it, Sprocket Player reads the photo library on your device to show your photos and videos. They are displayed on the device and are not copied or sent anywhere.
policy.crash.title: Crash reports
policy.crash.p1: Crash reporting is off by default. Nothing is collected unless you turn on Share Crash Reports in Options, and you can turn it off again at any time.
policy.crash.p2_before: If you turn it on, crash and hang reports are sent to
policy.crash.p2_after: , a crash-reporting service, and stored in the European Union. They are used only to find and fix bugs. A report contains:
policy.crash.li1: technical details of the failure, such as stack traces and the state of the app at that moment
policy.crash.li2: the device model, operating system version and app version
policy.crash.p3: Reports are not linked to your identity and are not used for tracking. They contain no screenshots, no media files, no sign-in details and nothing from your photo library. The app does not record usage sessions or performance traces.
policy.children.title: Children's privacy
policy.children.body: Sprocket Player is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect personal information from children.
